events_chronological: Years earlier in a far country, gangsters hold the family of a criminal known as Varga hostage, and he kills his own wife and children and then everyone connected to the men, and disappears into legend.
Five criminals - Deane, Corbin, Lasko, Riis and Willem Kade - are pulled into a hijacking lineup and held overnight in the same cell.
In the cell they plan revenge on a police escort racket, a ring of corrupt officers moving smugglers across the city.
The crew ambush the escort, and the ensuing scandal tears the department apart.
Deane's lawyer and lover Rhea Dolan gets them out to the coast, where Corbin's contact Whit buys the stolen jewels.
Whit puts them on to a jeweller who turns out to be a courier carrying heroin, and the crew realise they are being steered.
A lawyer named Vasiliev appears, says he acts for Varga, tells each man he has unknowingly stolen from Varga, and orders them to destroy a boatload of his rivals' cocaine.
Lasko runs and is found shot dead on a beach.
The crew try to kill Vasiliev in his office and back off when he reveals he is holding Rhea.
On the night of the raid the four survivors board the rival's boat in the harbour.
Riis and Corbin are killed below decks, and there is no cocaine anywhere on the ship.
Deane is shot by a figure on deck while Kade watches from the dockside, and the boat goes up in flames.
An investigator named Dagg questions Kade in a borrowed police office by the harbour, pressing him to give up Deane.
A burned survivor tells investigators from his hospital bed that Varga was on the boat, and begins describing him to a sketch artist.
Kade, granted immunity, tells Dagg that Deane was Varga all along, collects his belongings and walks out of the station.
Dagg realises that Kade improvised the entire story from the noticeboard behind the desk and the maker's name on the bottom of a coffee cup.
Kade's limp and his crippled hand straighten out as he walks down the street, and Vasiliev collects him in a waiting car.
The faxed sketch finishes printing, and the face on it is Kade's.
nonlinear_category_reason: The interrogation is the narrating present and everything else is the survivor's flashback, with one further flashback nested inside it.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a flash-forward to the night of the raid, which the film only catches up with at told-order bullets 13-14. Everything from bullet 3 to bullet 14 is the survivor's narration, a long flashback nested inside the interrogation of bullet 2, and bullet 9 is a flashback within that flashback, reaching years further back into the legend. The final bullets reveal that the whole structure was improvised.
fabula_notes: The narrator is unreliable, so most of this chronology is his invention rather than the story world's; the ordering follows the account he gives, which the closing bullets expose as assembled on the spot from objects in the office. The massacre in the far country is delivered as legend rather than witnessed, and the identity of the man who shoots the crew leader is left for the audience to infer.

events.content: Men holding a criminal's wife and children on the floor of his own house tell him what he is going to sign. He shoots his family himself, tells the men to go and bury their own, and then kills everyone any of them ever knew.
events.location: a house in a far country

reader: intro:Varga
a name exists that nobody in the trade will say out loud

events.content: Five men who have never worked together are pulled in on a hijacking that none of them did, made to stand in a line and read a sentence off a card, and then left overnight in one cell.

reader: intro:Deane
intro:Corbin
intro:Lasko
intro:Riis
intro:Kade

questions.q8: why were these particular five men put in one room?

events.content: By the small hours the talk has moved from grievance to arithmetic, and one of them lays out the racket where uniformed officers drive smugglers across the city for a fee.

reader: a crew forms out of a night in a cell

events.content: They take the convoy at a set of lights, put the officers face down on the tarmac and photograph everything. What follows in the newspapers takes the department apart from the top.

reader: the crew's first job is a public humiliation of the police

events.content: The lawyer who has been getting one of them out of things for years arranges the flight and the buyer, and a man on a pier counts the stones out under a lamp and pays in cash.

reader: intro:Rhea
intro:Whit

events.content: The buyer puts them on to an easy jeweller who turns out to be carrying heroin instead of stones, and afterwards the four of them sit in a room working out that every job they have taken was handed to them.
events.location: a rented room on the coast

reader: the crew's luck has been arranged from outside

questions.q7: who has been putting the work in front of them?

events.content: A lawyer with a soft voice and a briefcase visits each of them separately, recites something out of his own past that he could not possibly know, tells him whose money he has been stealing, and names the boat.

reader: intro:Vasiliev
the crew are now working for the name

questions.q2: who is the man this lawyer says he acts for?

events.content: One of them decides the whole thing is a story and goes. He is found the next morning on a beach a long way up the coast with sand in his mouth and two entry wounds.

reader: the first man to test whether the name is real does not come back

events.content: They get into his office with the door locked behind them and a gun against his ear, and he does not move at all, and then reads out an address and a description of what she was wearing that morning.

reader: the crew are held by the one person any of them loves

events.content: Four of them come over the rail at the harbour end after dark, in the rain, with the crew of the ship already at their stations and nobody yet shouting.

reader: the job everybody has been steered towards is beginning

questions.q6: what is actually on that ship?

events.content: It goes wrong below decks in a corridor too narrow to turn round in. Both of them are dead within a minute, and the men who go through the hold afterwards find fuel, water, and no drugs anywhere on the ship.

reader: the cargo everybody came for was never there

events.content: A man walks the deck as though he owns it and shoots the crew leader in the back of the head without breaking stride. On the dockside one of them watches it happen and does not move, and then the boat goes up.

reader: the killing is witnessed by exactly one person who survives

questions.q3: who is the man walking about on that deck?

events.content: An investigator borrows an office by the harbour with a cluttered noticeboard and a coffee pot, sits the survivor down, and works on him for a whole afternoon to give up the crew leader.
events.location: a borrowed office by the harbour

reader: intro:Dagg
the account of everything so far is being produced under pressure

questions.q1: what actually happened on that boat?

events.content: A man burned over most of his body says, through the tube in his throat and an interpreter, that the name was on the boat, and then works with an artist on the face for as long as he can stay awake.

reader: intro:the burned survivor
a face is being drawn somewhere else in the building

questions.q4: whose face is the burned man describing?

events.content: With immunity signed he delivers the ending: the crew leader was the name all along, and everything else follows from that. Then he signs for his watch, his lighter and his cigarettes and is walked to the door.

Dagg: a version he can write up
reader: the story closes neatly on a dead man who cannot contradict it

questions.q5: was any of what he said true?

events.content: He is turning the cup in his hand when he sees the maker's name on the bottom of it, and then the board behind the desk, and every name and place from the afternoon is on it, and the cup goes on the floor.

Dagg: the whole account was assembled from the objects in the room
reader: the narration was improvised in front of them

events.content: Twenty yards down the pavement the limp goes out of the walk. The crippled hand opens, finds a lighter, and works it, and a car pulls in at the kerb with the soft-voiced lawyer already holding the door.

reader: the injuries were part of the performance

events.content: The machine in the corner finishes the last band of the picture and the sheet curls off it, and the face looking up off the paper is the one that just walked out of the building.

Dagg: who he has just let go
reader: the name and the witness are the same man
